newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-LIFE BAN UPHELD ON BRIBE CHARGE REFEREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIFE BAN UPHELD ON BRIBE CHARGE REFEREE.

text.p: Swiss referee Kurt Roethlisberger, once recognised as one of soccer's top officials, had his appeal against a life ban for attempted bribery rejected by UEFA on Thursday.

Roethlisberger was suspended two weeks ago after a UEFA investigation found he had solicited a bribe to fix a European Champions' League match between Grasshopper Zurich and French champions Auxerre on October 30.
Since the decision, Roethlisberger, who officiated at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups and the 1988 Seoul Olympics during a 27-year career, had steadfastly maintained his innocence.
But the UEFA Board of Appeals, rejected the 46-year-old schoolteacher's explanation of the events and stood by their original ruling.

"I knew from the start that UEFA could make no other decision," said Roethlisberger before a swarm of television cameras, including Swiss TV which interupted programming to broadcast the post-hearing interview. "It's my word against their's.
"I feel I am a victim. I was used as an example to others who really are corrupt."
Roethlisberger was alleged to have approached Grasshopper manager Erich Vogel and asked if he was interested in having the referee, Vadim Zhuk of Belarus, favouring the Zurich club.
Roethlisberger told Vogel he was friendly with the referee and that it would be easy to arrange the matter for the sum of 100,000 Swiss Francs ($68,000).
The hearing, which lasted nearly 12 hours, was held under unusually tight security at a Geneva airport hotel.
The five-member UEFA panel questioned all the key figures involved, including Roethlisberger and Zhuk.

"Mr. Vogel expressed himself clearly and without contradiction," said UEFA deputy secretary Markus Studer, reading from a nine page document. "In contrast the Board of Appeals found the statements made by Roethlisberger to be inconsistent and not convincing.
"At first he denied everything and then later admitted wrongdoing.
"Mr. Roethlisberger has seriously abused his role and damaged the image of his profession.
"It is for those reasons that the Board of Appeals approved the sentence handed down by the Control and Disciplinary Committee."
Zhuk remains under suspension while his involvement is investigated. His case is expected to come up at the next UEFA Control and Disciplinary meeting.
